prompt:
Edit this production 3x3 texture atlas for a shooting guide. ONLY CHANGE THE LIGHTING AND CAST SHADOWS to be much more readable. Keep the exact character identity, fair skin material, black ponytail, matte sculpted 3D clay style, shirt, head angle, facial expression, framing, panel positions, background layout, and seamless exactly three columns by three rows with NO gutters, margins, text or borders. The output must remain square and all nine tiles equally sized. Do not add labels or sun icons. Preserve neutral closed mouths in columns1 and3 and gentle closed-mouth smiles in column2. Preserve head35degrees toward image-left in column3 and frontal in columns1/2.
Problem to fix: all faces currently look softly and evenly lit, so they do not teach sunlight direction. Make the contrast substantially stronger, with physical facial form shadows and distinct nose/jaw shadows, not a flat half-face color overlay.
ROW1, direct sunlight from UPPER IMAGE-LEFT, about45degrees off camera axis: clearly illuminated image-left forehead, left cheek and nose ridge. A distinct crisp-edged nose shadow falls DOWN AND TO IMAGE-RIGHT onto the opposite cheek; image-right eye socket and cheek are visibly darker. Strong readable shadow beneath the chin falls on neck and upper shirt. The lit cheek and shadow cheek should differ by about1.5stops. Warm neutral sunlight with cooler ambient fill in shadows. Facial features still readable.
ROW2, side sunlight from IMAGE-RIGHT at roughly90degrees to camera: unmistakable split-lighting effect following facial anatomy. Image-right cheek and forehead are brightly lit, while image-left cheek, eye socket and left half of chin are at least2stops darker with muted cool blue-violet ambient fill. Sharp nose cast shadow falls image-left. Shadow beneath jaw and down the image-left neck is clearly defined. Turned portraits must obey the same world light direction relative to camera. This row must visibly show the OPPOSITE side illuminated from row1.
ROW3, BACKLIT: strong sunlight coming from BEHIND her and slightly upper left. The entire front of her face and shirt are uniformly visibly shaded, about1.5stops below the bright background. Clear narrow warm rim light around hair silhouette, ponytail, ears and shoulder edges. Keep the face readable via dim cool ambient daylight, but do NOT front-light or brighten it to match the upper rows. No big halo or washed-out white skin. Still a usable well-exposed illustration of backlighting, not a black silhouette.
Maintain the SAME intrinsic pale skin color across rows: differences must be caused by light and shadow only. Do not change skin tone or makeup. Lighting should be bold and educational, clearly recognizable even as a small150px card. Keep the appealing clay character and polished production quality.
